topStories.headline: H-E-B to Build a New Ennis Store More Than Twice the Size of the Current One
topStories.dek: The grocer announced plans for a 112,000-square-foot store at Sonoma Trail and Ennis Avenue, with construction beginning in mid-2027 and an opening projected for late 2028.
topStories.body:
H-E-B confirmed last week that it will replace its longtime Ennis store with a dramatically larger supermarket at the corner of North Sonoma Trail and East Ennis Avenue. The new building will cover approximately 112,000 square feet — more than double the footprint of the current location at 101 S. Clay Street, which has served the community for more than 50 years.

According to H-E-B, plans are moving through the permitting process, with construction expected to begin in mid-2027 and the store to open by late 2028. The existing downtown location will remain fully operational until the new store is ready, and no decisions have been made yet about what will happen to the Clay Street property afterward.

The new store will include a full-service pharmacy with a drive-through lane, curbside pickup with dedicated parking, home delivery, and an in-store South Flo Pizza counter. H-E-B also said the building's design will reflect the character and personality of Ennis.

Ennis, which the U.S. Census Bureau estimated at roughly 26,000 residents as of mid-2025 — an increase of more than 25 percent since April 2020 — has grown substantially since the current H-E-B first opened. Current store employees will have the opportunity to transition to the new location, with additional job postings to follow as the opening approaches.

topStories.headline: Ennis Voters Back Street Repair Sales Tax 72% to 28%
topStories.dek: With all precincts reporting from the November 3 special election, Ennis Proposition A passed by a wide margin, keeping the quarter-cent street maintenance tax alive through at least 2030.
topStories.body:
Ennis voters approved the reauthorization of the city's quarter-cent street maintenance and repair sales tax by a decisive margin of 72.05 percent to 27.95 percent on Election Day, November 3. With all precincts counted, 3,751 votes were cast in favor of Proposition A and 1,455 against, according to NBC DFW's results tracker.

The tax, which amounts to 25 cents on a $100 purchase, had been scheduled to expire on March 31, 2027. Reauthorization locks it in for another four years from the date of the election and does not raise the overall city sales tax rate, which remains at 2.0 percent. Had the measure failed, the combined city local rate would have dropped to 1.75 percent.

Since the tax first went into effect in April 2015, it has generated more than $13.9 million for street and sidewalk maintenance, including $1.47 million in fiscal year 2025–2026, according to city records. The special election was ordered by the City Commission in August under Ordinance No. 26-0804-B2.

topStories.headline: Ennis ISD Brings in Interim Superintendent and Names New Deputy Leader
topStories.dek: The school district announced two leadership changes in the same week: Keith Boles joins as interim superintendent starting November 4, and Trent Dowd comes aboard as deputy superintendent.
topStories.body:
Ennis ISD Board of Trustees President Bill Chapman announced on October 28 that Keith Boles would serve as interim superintendent, with Boles beginning work on November 4. The Ennis Daily News described Boles as a respected leader in education, though the district has not yet publicly detailed the circumstances that created the opening.

Separately, the district announced the appointment of Trent Dowd as the new deputy superintendent. Dowd brings more than 20 years of experience in education to the role, according to the district's website, and is featured prominently in current headlines on the Ennis ISD homepage.

The two appointments represent significant leadership movement at the top of the district heading into the second semester. Ennis ISD serves approximately 6,621 students across 12 campuses, according to the Texas Education Agency's most recent school report card data.

moreNews.headline: Ellis County Lifts Countywide Burn Ban
moreNews.body: The Ellis County Commissioners' Court voted to rescind the countywide burn ban at its regular meeting on October 13, 2026. The ban, which had been in place since July, is now lifted effective immediately, according to the county's official news flash.

moreNews.headline: Free Meals for All Ennis ISD Students This School Year
moreNews.body: All students enrolled in Ennis ISD are receiving free breakfast and lunch during the 2026–2027 school year through the federal Community Eligibility Program (CEP), the district announced on its website. The benefit applies to all 12 campuses and roughly 6,621 enrolled students.
